subject: general
question: Why can Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) sometimes exceed 100%?

options.text: Due to school mergers in rural areas
Due to inclusion of post-graduate students
Due to enrollment of learners outside the official age group
Because of errors in census data

solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to enrollment of learners outside the official age group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER):** GER is a statistical measure used to determine the percentage of students enrolled in a specific level of education, regardless of age, as compared to the official age group corresponding to that level.
 
• GER can exceed **100%** when students outside the official age group enroll in schools or educational institutions. For example, older learners who previously missed out on education or younger students enrolling earlier can contribute to GER exceeding 100%. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The inclusion of learners outside the age group indicates that the educational system accommodates students who are not in the typical age range for a specific level of education. This is common in cases of adult education or delayed enrollment.
